I will do this year much like I did last year, with a small adjustment if the weather turns dry. I only have 2 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still would rather not let the crop go hungry. Around here, I watch what the good growers do. If a neighbor gets a full wheat head and a strong maize cob, I remember what he put down and I follow close to that. For wheat, I will keep using improved seed because the old seed does not fill as well now. I will put most of the base fertilizer in before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when the wheat turns green and again before jointing if the stand looks pale. With my well, I will give wheat three waters in a normal year: one after sowing if the ground is dry, one at greening, and one around jointing or heading. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people here, because the cobs are steadier and the yield is safer. I will put fertilizer under or beside the row, then add more nitrogen around the big bell-mouth stage. I will not be stingy with weed and insect control, because losing yield on 2 mu hurts more than spending a bit extra on one spray. I will keep rotary tillage because it is what I know, it is cheaper than deep ploughing every time, and it fits my small land and family labor.
